security_audit.summary: Most scanner hits are false positives from a generated Markdown transcript, Markdown backtick fences, and defensive secret-scan regexes. Confirmed risk remains because the active workflow reads local Codex session history, writes a transcript into the repository, and can push that transcript to a remote.

Show the target remote and branch before push, and require explicit approval when pushing a new upstream.
Replace the large committed transcript with a short sanitized example that omits historical shell command blocks.
Continue warning against raw JSONL commits and add a repository ignore rule for raw Codex session files.

content.user_title: Commit Code With Codex Session Provenance
content.value_statement: AI-assisted changes can lose the context that explains why code changed. This skill exports a redacted Codex transcript, commits it with the work, and pushes the branch.
actual_capabilities: Inspect Git status, diffs, branch, and remote information before staging.
Export a Markdown transcript from matching local Codex JSONL sessions.
Redact common secret formats and shorten home paths in exported transcripts.
Guide explicit staging, commit message selection, and cached diff review.
Push the current branch using the existing upstream or origin HEAD.
Warn against committing raw Codex session logs without explicit approval.
limitations: Redaction is not guaranteed to remove every secret or private detail.
The workflow assumes Git and Python are available in the local environment.
It can select the wrong session unless the repository path or session file is specified.
It does not resolve merge conflicts or rejected pushes without normal Git follow-up.

faq.question: Does this skill commit raw Codex session files?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to export a redacted Markdown transcript instead of raw JSONL logs.

faq.question: Can the transcript still contain sensitive data?
faq.answer: Yes. Redaction is a helper, so the transcript must be reviewed before staging.

faq.question: What tools does the workflow expect?
faq.answer: It expects Git, Python, and ripgrep for the recommended secret scan.

faq.question: How does it choose a Codex session?
faq.answer: The exporter selects the newest local session that appears to match the repository path.

faq.question: Can I choose a specific session file?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow supports passing a specific session path to the exporter.

faq.question: Does it push automatically in every case?
faq.answer: It guides Codex to push after review, using the existing upstream or origin HEAD when appropriate.
